subject: POST-R1 (RULED s323, first compiler item): writes_args fact on sub_info → arg-to-writer boxing; then delete lib/File/Basename.pm
description:
Fable ruling (fable-answers-s323.md §1): shape APPROVED with amendments — write set must include foreach-over-@_ aliasing, lvalue substr/vec/pos on $_[N], and ESCAPES (\$_[N], \@_, bare &callee;, goto &sub, @_ passed on): anything not provably read-only sets writes_args=1. Carry on sub_info (same channel as #77 returns; migrates to E5 Facts later — do NOT wait for E5). Consume as VarAnnotator reason `arg-to-writer` at same-file known-callee call sites first; cross-file later via _extract_module_prototypes. The "Cannot modify non-boxed value" warning STAYS as backstop for undetected writers. Guard BOTH directions (aliasing works at flagged sites; unflagged subs' args stay raw). NO blanket boxing of call args. Timing: POST-R1, ahead of perf work. Delete lib/File/Basename.pm when it lands.

s328 NOTE — the escape list must cover the CODE-REF goto spellings too, not just `goto &sub`: s328 made `goto \&NAME` / `goto $coderef` / `goto $h->{cb}` real tail calls (they were silent no-ops), so all of them now pass the live @_ on to the target and are escapes by the same argument. Measured then, as the guard rows to write:

  sub writer  { $_[0] = "WRITTEN" }
  my $v = "orig"; writer($v);                       # A direct
  sub a { goto &writer  } a($w);                    # B
  sub b { goto \&writer } b($x);                    # C
  my $cr = \&writer; sub c { goto $cr } c($y);      # D

perl writes through on ALL FOUR; PCL on none — including A, the plain direct call, which is exactly this task. So the goto paths are no worse than the baseline, and fixing #189 should make all four flip together. If A passes and B-D do not after the fix, the escape set missed the goto spellings.
